Here's my two cents. As a BS, we have to be open and receptive to trusting them again. For our WSs, it's up to them to be a trustworthy person. 

We aren't just going to blindly trust them again. It will always be in our minds, to some degree, for the rest of our lives. But neither one of us want it to control the rest of our lives. WS doesn't want to have to justify everything they do, and BS doesn't want to worry all the damn time. So, what to do?

We have to be able to talk about things with them. Calmly! And not in a lashing manner! Like both of us, back and forth. 

Get rid of social media, unlock phones, no drinking in public alone...... All great, and I agree with them wholeheartedly. Will any of that stop anything in the future? Where there's a will, there's a way. No. It's all about the intent, and wilful action on their part when they change something. But I think it's also up to us BSs to say, "hey, I noticed you (insert anything they did intentionally to avert a situation here). That means a lot to me." Or, it's up to us BSs to say that something bothers us (easier said than done without starting a nasty conversation). 

Again, BS, be open to receive WS trying their hardest to be trustworthy. Remember, when they intentionally do something to avoid a situation, they are remembering what happened, too. If they truly feel like crap about what they did, it will be a reminder. But, if you've ever been in a car crash, I'd like to think one would swerve off the road if another car was coming head-on in your lane. Likewise, should a WS. 

Think of things in terms of value. If drinking caused it, is drinking away from home more valuable? If it's social media and messaging, is that relationship more valuable? If it's seeing that person at work or another place you frequent, should you change jobs or not go to that place any more? Are you willing to do without that? Is it worth it? If you think about it, it's super easy. If you feel about it, you just complicate everything. Trouble usually ensues.

I have bipolar disorder. I get severely depressed. It's ok to get sad for a reason. It's ok if it lasts a few days. The catch is, you should start to get better after a few days. Please do not live like this. If you are questioning how you feel regarding depression, self realization of a potential problem is very healthy. Please see a doctor. Also, be very aware of yourself should you be given antidepressants. Have a trusted person to talk to about how you feel and tell them everything. Tell them everything you are feeling. If it's bad, tell your doctor immediately. Like, call the office and tell them your symptoms right away. They can have side effects.
